title: Zepto's IPO Valuation May Fall 27 Percent Below Peak as Profitability Concerns Mount
excerpt: Zepto's IPO valuation may drop to $5.1 billion, a 27% decrease from its peak.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Zepto's IPO valuation may drop to $5.1 billion, a 27% decrease from its peak.
  • Institutional interest remains strong, with major funds expected to anchor 40-45% of the IPO.
  • Zepto's net loss increased to Rs 5,095 crore, despite nearly doubling operating revenue.
  • Advertising revenue reached Rs 1,636 crore, indicating potential for improved profitability.
  • The IPO's pricing will influence the broader Indian tech market amid geopolitical uncertainties.

Quick Commerce Giant Faces Valuation Reality Check

Zepto, India's fast-growing quick commerce company, may make its stock market debut at a valuation significantly below its peak private valuation of $7 billion, as investors weigh concerns over cash burn, profitability, and broader geopolitical uncertainty.

Foreign investors have indicated interest at a pre-money valuation of approximately $4.5 billion, implying a post-money valuation of roughly $5.1 billion, according to Inc42. The potential 27 percent discount reflects a broader market shift toward prioritizing profitability over growth.

Strong Institutional Interest Despite Discount

Despite the valuation haircut, the IPO is attracting significant institutional interest. Norway's sovereign wealth fund Norges and Motilal Oswal are expected to account for 40 to 45 percent of Zepto's anchor book.

Zepto filed its updated DRHP for an IPO comprising a fresh issue worth Rs 8,010 crore and an OFS of up to 11.35 crore shares. Proceeds will fund dark store expansion, technology infrastructure, and marketing.

The Profitability Question

Zepto's net loss widened to Rs 5,095 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,697 crore in the prior year, even as operating revenue nearly doubled to Rs 22,624 crore. However, unit economics showed improvement — adjusted EBITDA loss per order narrowed to Rs 79 from Rs 136, while free cash flow burn per order declined to Rs 68 from Rs 161.

Advertising revenue emerged as a significant contributor at Rs 1,636 crore, pointing to high-margin streams that could accelerate the profitability path. The company also launched Zepto Club, an invite-only membership at Rs 99 per month offering cashback, free delivery, and priority service.

The Bigger Picture for Indian Tech IPOs

Zepto's pricing will serve as a barometer for India's new-age tech IPO market. After several high-profile listings fell below issue price, investors are demanding clearer profitability paths. Geopolitical uncertainty — including the US-Iran conflict and trade tensions — has added volatility.

For NRI investors who have watched quick commerce transform how their families in India shop for groceries, Zepto's public debut offers a chance to invest in a business model they understand intimately. Whether the valuation discount represents a buying opportunity or a warning sign depends on how quickly the company closes the gap between rapid revenue growth and sustainable profitability.

Sources: Inc42, Bloomberg, Moneycontrol
